findings.highlight: Whenever I tell her I love her, whenever I embrace her, whenever I betray her…
findings.evidenceJa:
雪菜へと愛を語ろうとすると。
雪菜を抱きしめようとすると。
雪菜を裏切ろうとすると…
findings.explanation: Haruki's body reacts when he tries to speak love, embrace, or betray Setsuna; the English turns attempts into habitual completed acts — The bodily breakdown around each possibility remains clear.
findings.japanese:
雪菜へと愛を語ろうとすると。
雪菜を抱きしめようとすると。
雪菜を裏切ろうとすると…
findings.todokanai: Whenever I tell her I love her, whenever I embrace her, whenever I betray her…

findings.highlight: when I chased her out of her apartment just so I could have Setsuna stay over
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜を部屋に泊めるためにかずさを部屋から追い出しておいて、『かずさの求める俺』もないもんだ…
findings.explanation: Haruki expelled Kazusa from his own apartment so Setsuna could stay there. The English says he drove Kazusa out of her apartment, reversing the location and obscuring the degrading command whose violation has just been revealed.
findings.japanese:
雪菜を部屋に泊めるために
かずさを部屋から追い出しておいて、
『かずさの求める俺』もないもんだ…
findings.todokanai: Though I suppose I can't call myself the me that Kazusa desires when I chased her out of her apartment just so I could have Setsuna stay over.

findings.highlight: Every time she calls out to me in that enticingly seductive way
findings.evidenceJa: わざといやらしい言葉を連発して挑発するたびに。
findings.explanation: Kazusa deliberately fires off one obscene phrase after another to provoke Haruki. The English replaces her explicit dirty talk and conscious provocation with a generally seductive manner of calling to him, flattening the strategy by which she tries to assume all blame for the sex.
findings.japanese: わざといやらしい言葉を連発して挑発するたびに。
findings.todokanai: Every time she calls out to me in that enticingly seductive way…

findings.highlight: As long as you pick me every now and then, I'll think of myself as lucky for that day.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ただ、たまたまあたしを選んでくれたら、今日はラッキーだったなって思うだけだ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that if Haruki happens, by chance, to choose her, she will simply count that day as lucky. 'Every now and then' turns her self-effacing acceptance of accident into a request for periodic access or rotation.
findings.japanese:
「ただ、たまたまあたしを選んでくれたら、
今日はラッキーだったなって思うだけだ」
findings.todokanai: "As long as you pick me every now and then, I'll think of myself as lucky for that day."

findings.highlight: they were still too much to include in an article
findings.evidenceJa: 毒にも薬にもならないかずさの述懐は、けれど、インタビュー記事としては十分すぎる内容だった。
findings.explanation: Kazusa's neutral recollections are more than sufficient material for an interview article. The English says they are too much to include, reversing Haruki's professional assessment and the reason he later returns for his recorder.
findings.japanese:
毒にも薬にもならないかずさの述懐は、
けれど、インタビュー記事としては十分すぎる内容だった。
findings.todokanai: Kazusa's recollections were neither poison nor antidote, yet they were still too much to include in an article.

findings.highlight: Touma Youko's tutor
findings.evidenceJa: マーティン・フリューゲル。冬馬曜子、かずさ母子の師匠にして、現代クラシック音楽界の系譜に必ず出てくる演奏家の一人。
findings.explanation: Martin Fluegel is the master of both Youko and Kazusa, the Touma mother and daughter. The English identifies him only as Youko's tutor, omitting his direct mentorship of Kazusa—the relationship driving his warning and the entire recollection.
findings.japanese:
マーティン・フリューゲル。
冬馬曜子、かずさ母子の師匠にして、
現代クラシック音楽界の系譜に必ず出てくる演奏家の一人。
findings.todokanai: Martin Fluegel. Touma Youko's tutor, and a name that always comes up during the topic of modern classical music.

findings.highlight: I find myself calming down at the prospect
findings.evidenceJa: …そんな歴史的偉人も、口の悪い愛弟子たちにかかれば、『ただの口うるさい爺さん』という庶民的な表現に落ち着いてしまう。
findings.explanation: The narration jokes that even a historic giant becomes merely 'a nagging old man' once his foul-mouthed favorite pupils are through describing him. The English invents Haruki calming down, misassigning the predicate and losing the high-to-low-register joke.
findings.japanese:
…そんな歴史的偉人も、口の悪い愛弟子たちにかかれば、
『ただの口うるさい爺さん』という庶民的な表現に
落ち着いてしまう。
findings.todokanai: …I find myself calming down at the prospect that even a grand and historical man such as him is "nothing but an annoying old man" to his foul-mouthed favorite students.

findings.highlight: Do you think I'm being too clingy?
findings.evidenceJa: 「刷り込みだって思うか？『いつか必ず俺よりもっといい男が現れる』って、そんなくだらない台詞、言うか？」
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks whether Haruki dismisses her lifelong fixation as imprinting—the first available man becoming permanently encoded. 'Too clingy' removes the psychological concept and breaks her following defense that her world was broad but only Haruki truly chose her.
findings.japanese:
「刷り込みだって思うか？
『いつか必ず俺よりもっといい男が現れる』って、
そんなくだらない台詞、言うか？」
findings.todokanai: "Do you think I'm being too clingy? Are you going to tell me something worthless like, 'You'll find a better guy than me one day?'…?"

findings.highlight: I'm just one of many guys who happened to be near you five years ago
findings.evidenceJa: 「俺はただ、五年前にかずさの目の前にいた、唯一の男ってだけで…それ以外のことなんか、なにも」
findings.explanation: Haruki calls himself merely the one and only man who stood before Kazusa five years ago. The English says he was one of many, directly reversing the premise Kazusa spends the entire exchange defending.
findings.japanese:
「俺はただ、五年前にかずさの目の前にいた、
唯一の男ってだけで…
それ以外のことなんか、なにも」
findings.todokanai: "I'm just one of many guys who happened to be near you five years ago… nothing more than that."

findings.highlight: It was because she was special that she tried to avert her gaze from it.
findings.evidenceJa: 特別であるが故に、その特別から敢えて目を逸らしてた。
findings.explanation: The surrounding students deliberately looked away from Kazusa's specialness because it intimidated, inspired envy, or provoked hatred. The English makes Kazusa herself avert her gaze, severing the explanation for why hundreds surrounded her but only Haruki faced and chose her.
findings.japanese:
特別であるが故に、
その特別から敢えて目を逸らしてた。
findings.todokanai: It was because she was special that she tried to avert her gaze from it.

findings.highlight: picked you out of all the hundreds of guys she could have picked
findings.evidenceJa: 「雪菜はさ…自分を選んだ数百人の男の中からお前を選んだ」
findings.explanation: Setsuna chose Haruki from among hundreds of men who had chosen her. The English says merely that she could have picked hundreds, losing the reciprocal structure: Setsuna was widely chosen, whereas Kazusa says only one man ever chose her.
findings.japanese:
「雪菜はさ…
自分を選んだ数百人の男の中からお前を選んだ」
findings.todokanai: "Setsuna… picked you out of all the hundreds of guys she could have picked."

findings.highlight: I… had no one else to pick but you from the very start.
findings.evidenceJa: 「けどあたしはさ…最初からお前一人にしか選ばれなかったんだよ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says that from the beginning Haruki was the only person who chose her. The English says Haruki was the only person available for Kazusa to choose, reversing agent and patient and destroying the contrast with Setsuna in line 254.
findings.japanese:
「けどあたしはさ…
最初からお前一人にしか選ばれなかったんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "But I… had no one else to pick but you from the very start."

findings.highlight: We don't have to go all the way. We can just remain like this… I'll be as happy as I can until it's over.
findings.evidenceJa: 「実を結ばなくてもいい。花を咲かせるだけでいい。…散るまでの時間を、精一杯幸せに過ごすから」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says their love need not bear fruit; merely flowering is enough, and she will spend the time until the petals fall as happily as she can. The English deletes the sustained botanical image, which line 292 then extends from flower to a new sprout and possible child.
findings.japanese:
「実を結ばなくてもいい。花を咲かせるだけでいい。
…散るまでの時間を、精一杯幸せに過ごすから」
findings.todokanai: "We don't have to go all the way. We can just remain like this… I'll be as happy as I can until it's over."

findings.highlight: didn't feel all that warm
findings.evidenceJa: 毒にも薬にもならないはずのかずさの言葉は、やっぱり俺にとって、そんな生温いものであるはずもなく。
findings.explanation: Kazusa's supposedly neutral words could never be anything so lukewarm, mild, or harmless to Haruki. The English literally denies warmth, suggesting coldness instead of overwhelming emotional potency and breaking the poison-or-medicine frame.
findings.japanese:
毒にも薬にもならないはずのかずさの言葉は、
やっぱり俺にとって、そんな生温いものであるはずもなく。
findings.todokanai: In the end, the words Kazusa spoke, which were supposed to be neither poison nor antidote, didn't feel all that warm.

findings.highlight: I lose my strength, and invite Kazusa with me to oblivion.
findings.evidenceJa: かずさのなかに包まれたままの俺は、少しずつ力を失い、俺たちを終焉へと誘う。
findings.explanation: Still enveloped inside Kazusa, Haruki gradually loses his erection and brings their prolonged intercourse to its end. The English says he and Kazusa are being invited to oblivion, replacing a concrete sexual transition with unsupported melodrama.
findings.japanese:
かずさのなかに包まれたままの俺は、
少しずつ力を失い、俺たちを終焉へと誘う。
findings.todokanai: So as I lie down while being held by Kazusa, I lose my strength, and invite Kazusa with me to oblivion.

findings.highlight: If you could send me not a flower, but a new sprout
findings.evidenceJa: 「花だけでなく、新しい芽を吹かせてくれたら…そしたらあたし、もっともっと、幸せに…」
findings.explanation: Extending her earlier metaphor, Kazusa says that if Haruki let not only a flower bloom but also a new bud sprout, she would be happier still—an oblique wish for pregnancy. The English changes 'not only the flower, but also' into 'not a flower, but,' making the new life replace rather than grow from their flowering love.
findings.japanese:
「花だけでなく、新しい芽を吹かせてくれたら…
そしたらあたし、もっともっと、幸せに…」
findings.todokanai: "If you could send me not a flower, but a new sprout… then I'd be even happier."

findings.highlight: It's not that big of a deal for a journalist to be late.
findings.evidenceJa: 「なぁ、そんなに慌てなくても。出版業界なんて朝は遅刻しても平気なんじゃないのか？どうせ働き出すのは夜中だろ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa stereotypes the publishing industry as tolerant of late mornings because its work runs into the night. The English calls Haruki a journalist, changing his profession and the workplace culture being mocked.
findings.japanese:
「なぁ、そんなに慌てなくても。
出版業界なんて朝は遅刻しても平気なんじゃないのか？
どうせ働き出すのは夜中だろ」
findings.todokanai: "Hey, you don't have to be in such a rush. It's not that big of a deal for a journalist to be late. Most of your work is done at night, anyway."

findings.highlight: done along with professionals
findings.evidenceJa: 今回の特集号は、編プロと共同とは言え、俺が直接編集に携わるという意味で、記念すべき初仕事。
findings.explanation: The special issue is a joint project with an editorial-production company, 編プロ, not simply work done 'with professionals.' The English erases the subcontracting structure that makes this Haruki's first commemorative job with direct editorial responsibility.
findings.japanese:
今回の特集号は、編プロと共同とは言え、
俺が直接編集に携わるという意味で、記念すべき初仕事。
findings.todokanai: This current job might be one done along with professionals, but it's also my first job as a direct participant, which ought to be commemorated.

findings.highlight: Everything is going at a rapid pace already from the beginning of the week. There's no point in even thinking about taking sick leave.
findings.evidenceJa:
週の初めからものすごいペースだな。
リハビリなんて言ってる場合じゃない。
findings.explanation: Haruki says there is no time to ease back into work or rehabilitate; 'taking sick leave' is a different employment action — The punishing pace and abandoned recovery remain clear.
findings.japanese:
週の初めからものすごいペースだな。
リハビリなんて言ってる場合じゃない。
findings.todokanai: Everything is going at a rapid pace already from the beginning of the week. There's no point in even thinking about taking sick leave.

findings.highlight: it'll look like I'm trying to make up for my lack of natural skill
findings.evidenceJa: 「そう書かれると、母さんに比べてあたしが随分と小者に見えるな」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says the comparison makes her look like a decidedly smaller figure or small fry beside Youko. The English invents compensating for deficient talent, while subsequent lines translate the repeated 小者 exchange as 'upstart' and 'inferior,' destroying the affectionate joke that industrious Kazusa and protective Haruki are both petty little mortals beside the effortless genius.
findings.japanese:
「そう書かれると、
母さんに比べてあたしが随分と小者に見えるな」
findings.todokanai: "If you write that, it'll look like I'm trying to make up for my lack of natural skill."
